convert_tool_src = await read_file("./skills/OfficeBench/tools/word/convert_to_pdf.py")

# The tool uses LibreOffice which isn't available. Let me write a custom Python script
# that uses python-docx to read the content and reportlab/fpdf to create a PDF.
# Since we have PyMuPDF (fitz) installed, I'll use a different approach:
# Read the docx paragraphs and write them to a PDF using fitz (PyMuPDF).

script_content = """\
import fitz  # PyMuPDF
from docx import Document

# Read the Word document
doc = Document("/workspace/testbed/docs/customer_report.docx")

# Create a new PDF
pdf = fitz.open()

# Page dimensions (A4)
page_width = 595
page_height = 842
margin = 50
usable_width = page_width - 2 * margin
y_position = margin
line_height = 14
title_line_height = 20

# Add first page
page = pdf.new_page(width=page_width, height=page_height)

for para in doc.paragraphs:
    text = para.text.strip()
    if not text:
        y_position += line_height / 2
        continue

    # Determine font size based on style
    style_name = para.style.name if para.style else "Normal"
    if "Title" in style_name or "Heading 1" in style_name:
        fontsize = 16
        current_line_height = title_line_height + 4
    elif "Heading 2" in style_name:
        fontsize = 14
        current_line_height = title_line_height
    elif "Heading" in style_name:
        fontsize = 12
        current_line_height = line_height + 4
    else:
        fontsize = 10
        current_line_height = line_height

    # Check if we need a new page
    if y_position + current_line_height > page_height - margin:
        page = pdf.new_page(width=page_width, height=page_height)
        y_position = margin

    # Insert text
    text_point = fitz.Point(margin, y_position + fontsize)
    page.insert_text(text_point, text, fontsize=fontsize, fontname="helv")
    y_position += current_line_height

# Save the PDF
output_path = "/workspace/testbed/docs/customer_report.pdf"
pdf.save(output_path)
pdf.close()
print(f"PDF saved to {output_path}")
"""
